item.title: Campaigners back call for scrutiny of consent laws by Joanne Young

item.title: ‘So what if there’s a hole? It hasn’t collapsed’: Kyiv residents unbothered by Russian attacks on city’s bridges
item.author: Dan Sabbagh in Kyiv; photographs by Julia Kochetova
item.content:encoded: Despite dodging tears in the tarmac, people are confident in city’s infrastructure – and will not worry about what has not happened yetMykola expects to drive his battered beige passenger minibus 20 to 24 times a day past the holes in the road on Kyiv’s damaged Northern Bridge that were caused by a Russian ballistic missile attack on Tuesday.Buses are now the only motor transport allowed across the normally busy multi-lane crossing, though on their way into the city centre they have to skirt the tears in the tarmac, using the only functioning lane to get by.Continue reading...

item.title: Tourists are throwing fewer coins into Rome’s Trevi fountain – is €2 entry fee to blame?

item.content:encoded: Charity that collects the coins says donations are down by £200,000 after a barrier was put in place to restrict accessWhen Jeff Clinton, an American visiting Rome with his wife for the first time, found a US one-cent coin on a street close to Termini train station, he knew precisely what he was going to do with it. “I’ll throw it into the Trevi fountain,” said Clinton, holding the copper coin in the palm of his hand as the couple admired the landmark.He was well aware of the tradition among tourists of tossing a coin over their shoulder and into the waters of the baroque masterpiece, in a ritual fabled to ensure a return visit to the city or make other dreams come true.Continue reading...

item.title: When you see smoke, run: Rohingya who escaped Myanmar’s genocide tell their stories

item.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
item.author: Alice Nightingale-Smith for MetDesk
item.content:encoded: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recordedMultiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.Continue reading...

Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.Continue reading...

item.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
item.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
item.content:encoded: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in GazaThe ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.Continue reading...
